titel: Why shellfish turn red when cooked
kurz: The shells of prawns, crabs and lobster contain a red pigment wrapped up grey-blue by a protein. Heat undoes the wrapping and the red appears.
bild_im_kopf: Like a red present in grey wrapping paper: only when you tear the paper open do you see the colour.
was_passiert: The pigment is called astaxanthin and is actually red. In the living animal it is bound to a protein that makes it look blue-grey. When heated this protein changes ([[eiweiss-denaturierung|denaturation]]) and lets the pigment go. The free astaxanthin colours shell and flesh red and pink.
warum_wichtig: The colour reliably shows when prawns are cooked. The same pigment reaches salmon and trout through their diet and turns their flesh pink.
faustregeln: Prawns are done once they are pink throughout and no longer glassy.
Frying in the shell releases colour and flavour: the shells make a red stock or a shellfish oil.

stellschrauben.wirkung: Even moderate heat frees the pigment from the protein

praxis.text: Farmed salmon is fed astaxanthin, otherwise its flesh would stay pale.
